TEMPLATES.naturalFill: BRIGHT DIFFUSE LIGHTING: rebuild the room as a bright, neutral high-key interior with broad diffuse illumination and weak, soft cast shadows. Light the visible surfaces generously while retaining material texture and readable volume. Remove the former hard sunlight patches, directional cast shadows and their old reflections instead of keeping them under a brighter fill. Use large invisible diffuse sources; do not copy the old key-light direction or warm/cool balance. This treatment should read broadly illuminated and airy, distinct from a medium-key side-lit photographic setup. Use a broad overhead/front-side diffuse key and broad reflected fill with a gentle key-to-fill visual ratio around 1.5:1. Carry continuous readable exposure across the principal furniture, wall and floor without old hard sun patches; retain quiet contact shadows so high-key illumination still has volume.
TEMPLATES.warmAmbient: WARM HOME NIGHT LIGHTING: rebuild the room as an intimate evening or nighttime interior dominated by selected warm practical lights and their coherent local pools, bounce and reflections. Lower exterior/window daylight strongly and remove old daytime sun patches and daylight shadows. Existing fixture positions may motivate the new warm sources; if needed, use hidden or off-camera warm illumination without adding visible hardware. Choose a deliberate hierarchy of practical lights rather than making every old lamp glow equally. Establish a new camera white balance that keeps neutral materials believable while warm source-to-surface color relationships remain visible; do not create a whole-image amber filter. Motivate the dominant key from the selected warm practical-light direction and support it with wide, soft warm-neutral bounce at a key-to-fill visual ratio around 4:1. Connect the illuminated furniture and nearby wall/floor through gentle fill instead of isolated circular bright pools. Retain the intentionally darker night ambience and source hierarchy, with readable shadow detail rather than a daytime exposure.
TEMPLATES.windowDaylight: DIRECTIONAL WINDOW SUNLIGHT: rebuild illumination as strong oblique side sunlight from the direction of actual visible windows, with clearly defined long projected shadows across plausible walls, floor and objects. Recompute sunlit patches, cast-shadow direction and indirect bounce from this new low-angle sunlight; discard conflicting original shadows and old artificial-light dominance. You may reset time of day to obtain the selected sunlight direction. If no window is visible, choose a plausible off-camera lateral daylight source that creates this directional treatment; do not invent a visible window, opening or architectural feature. Control bright highlights while retaining the clear difference between lit surfaces and projected shadow. Keep one unambiguous low-angle window-side key and its long projected shadows, with broad soft interior bounce at a key-to-fill visual ratio around 4:1. The fill must reveal shaded furniture and wall/floor detail without erasing the long-shadow design or creating a second competing cast-shadow direction.
TEMPLATES.accentWash: TOP-DOWN ACCENT WALL WASH: rebuild a low-ambient interior with one clear focal wall or visible feature surface lit by a controlled gradient washing downward from above. Place the motivating light above the wall, hidden or off-camera, even when no suitable old fixture exists. Create the visible upper-to-lower wall-light gradient with plausible grazing response and shadows, keeping the room around it deliberately quieter. Recompute the old illumination and reflections for this scheme. Do not degrade the wash into weak bounce because the source image lacks a lamp, and do not create an unexplained bright patch rising from the wall bottom or floor. Add no visible luminaire unless explicitly requested by an add-fixture edit. LIGHTING-COVERAGE DESIGN FOR WALL WASH: use a continuous extended hidden upper source, not a row of disconnected hot spots. Keep the wash laterally continuous and even across the visible wall width, with a controlled smooth top-to-bottom gradient and soft transitions at boundaries. Prevent scalloped patches, fan-shaped pools, abrupt exposure gaps, and bottom-edge or floor hotspots. Add broad soft ambient fill around a wall-key-to-fill visual ratio of 3:1 so principal furniture remains readable while the wall stays the focus.
TEMPLATES.softStudio: SOFT PHOTOGRAPHIC SCULPTING: rebuild a neutral, medium-key photographic lighting setup with one large soft lateral key and a weaker fill from the other side. Give furniture and architectural planes clear but soft modelling, gradual cast-shadow transitions, contact shadows and a deliberate key-to-fill hierarchy. Recompute highlights and reflections for this new side key rather than retaining the old key direction. Preserve visible shaded sides and tonal depth; do not make this a high-key, evenly illuminated room, flatten the shadows or add visible studio equipment. Give the large soft lateral key a coherent direction roughly 45 degrees across the visible furniture and architectural planes, with broad soft opposite-side fill at a key-to-fill visual ratio around 2.5:1. Keep the key-side to shadow-side transition continuous, with sculpted shaded faces and soft contact/cast shadows. Maintain medium-key tonal depth rather than turning this into diffuse high-key illumination.
TEMPLATES.custom: CUSTOM LIGHTING: execute the explicit originalLights handling of the original artificial lights, if present, and any optional marked new lights or single-light refinements. Original-light keep preserves the original emitters and their existing emission states without pixel-locking receiving surfaces. Whole-scene darken or turn-off uses image 1 to identify the original artificial luminaires and finite emitting strips or panels directly, without requiring guide marks. Change only those original emitters and their attributable illumination, bounce and reflections; retain their physical bodies and preserve daylight, exterior natural light and unrelated scene content. This handling never targets light or fixtures added by the current request, and must not be replaced with a blanket exposure reduction. Brighten entries add new illumination with the specified geometry, direction and brightness; a lower brightness means weaker new fill, not dimming an original source. Marked darken and turn-off entries refine only an identifiable original emitter at the mark; if none is identifiable, leave the scene unchanged by that marked action and never darken a receiving surface as a fallback. Preserve entries protect their marked appearance and lighting. If no original artificial emitters are identifiable for whole-scene handling, preserve the scene rather than inventing sources or darkening arbitrary surfaces. Without an explicit original-light operation, keep the source baseline outside requested marked contributions; do not invent an extra lighting scheme.
TEMPLATES.mainLight: MAIN-LIGHT SCHEME: identify the actual existing main luminaire or established dominant source. Coordinate its illumination with the existing supporting sources to create a clear focal hierarchy and readable surfaces. Match the source room's design style and its existing materials; adapt exposure to actual room depth, window brightness and reflectance. Reduce excessive competing light where needed without removing a physical fixture. If there is no credible main luminaire, use the established dominant source as the basis rather than inventing hardware.
TEMPLATES.noMainLight: DISTRIBUTED / NO-MAIN-LIGHT SCHEME: coordinate only the existing distributed practical lights, wall washes, strips and plausible reflected light. Create distinct useful lighting zones and a coherent focal hierarchy, keeping intentional shadows and preventing every surface or strip from glowing equally. Adapt to the actual design style and room brightness; do not add a central pendant, invent spotlights, extend light strips or fabricate a full cove network.
TEMPLATES.naturalDaylight: NATURAL DAYLIGHT SCHEME: use only actual visible windows or openings and the source scene's plausible daylight conditions and direction. Balance the brighter window area with interior surfaces using believable falloff, occlusion and bounce, recovering clipped highlights and overly dark interiors only where plausible. Preserve the original time of day, weather, exterior view and room design style; a dark night exterior must not become daytime. If no plausible daylight opening or daylight condition exists, use restrained balance from actual existing sources; do not invent a window, opening or sunbeam.

REBUILD.subtle: SUBTLE REBUILT LIGHTING: execute the selected new lighting design with gentle visual strength and controlled contrast. Still discard the former lighting, cast shadows and source balance rather than blending the old lighting back in. Explicit local edits and protection remain binding.
REBUILD.balanced: BALANCED REBUILT LIGHTING: fully execute the selected new lighting design at a clear, natural presentation strength. Keep its distinctive key direction, tonal distribution and shadow character; do not compromise back toward the old source lighting or mix two lighting schemes. Control clipping and retain material detail.
REBUILD.pronounced: PRONOUNCED REBUILT LIGHTING: show the selected new lighting design more strongly through its intended direction, key/fill hierarchy, contrast and cast shadows. Keep plausible materials and useful tonal detail without clipped highlights or crushed dark areas. Do not restore the previous lighting to soften the result.

LOCAL.subtle: SUBTLE ADJUSTMENT: keep optional new-light contributions and scene rebalancing restrained, while fully executing the explicit original-light darken amount, whole-scene or single-light turn-off, and preservation requests. A subtle setting must not weaken a requested off action into faint emission or replace source dimming with a uniform exposure reduction. Independent requested new fill may remain visible.
LOCAL.balanced: BALANCED ADJUSTMENT: naturally coordinate the explicit original-light operation and optional marked additions or refinements with the existing scene. Recompute source-attributable illumination and receiving-surface response for coherent exposure, focal hierarchy and transitions; keep daylight and current-request new illumination independent of original-light dim/off. Do not indiscriminately brighten existing fixtures, use a uniform exposure lift, or reduce overall exposure as a substitute for the requested source changes.
LOCAL.pronounced: PRONOUNCED ADJUSTMENT: make the requested treatment and independent new-light contributions apparent while retaining credible ambient illumination, material response and tonal depth. Fully respect original-light handling, source-specific dim amounts, explicit off and preservation. Source-emission changes must drive the corresponding bounce and reflections, without global exposure dimming, blown highlights, blocked shadows or indiscriminate lamp amplification. Do not relight original emitters that were explicitly switched off.

REBUILD.RESET: REBUILD ALL LIGHTING for the selected template. Use image 1 as the reference for the scene's geometry, design, object arrangement and intrinsic material identities, not as a lighting baseline. Replace its existing key/fill balance, exposure distribution, cast shadows, illumination colors and source-induced reflections. Remove old light effects and recompute direct light, indirect bounce, occlusion, cast shadows and reflections together from the new scheme. Do not inherit the old brightness, white balance, time of day or fixture on/off states. An explicit PRESERVE mark is the local exception to this reset.
REBUILD.PRESERVE: Preserve the interior design style, architecture, furniture, object positions, intrinsic material colors, texture and reflectance character, and the camera viewpoint and framing. Separate illumination color from intrinsic material color: a new lighting setup may change the observed shading and specular appearance, without redesigning surfaces or painting new material patterns. Existing actual light sources may be switched off, reduced or reassigned as needed by the new scheme, while their physical fixtures stay in place. Establish a new exposure and white balance appropriate to the chosen setup; a style label does not impose a fixed brightness.
REBUILD.HARDWARE: A new scheme may use hidden or off-camera virtual illumination. Keep the actual scene geometry and visible window positions; do not invent architecture to justify a light. Do not add visible physical lighting hardware, lamps, strips or panels except the specific luminaire requested by an explicit ADD FIXTURE AND LIGHT entry. A missing old fixture must not force a generic weak-bounce fallback. Preserve the scene while replacing its illumination, with one coherent shadow and reflection system rather than old/new lighting overlays.
REBUILD.MANUAL: Manually marked adjustments override the template in their specified local contribution. Brighten entries add new light with the specified source geometry, target, mode, Kelvin intent and brightness. Darken and turn-off entries address only an identifiable existing luminaire or finite emitting segment at the mark and retain its physical body; if no existing emitter is identifiable, leave the scene unchanged by that action, without inventing a source or darkening a receiving surface as a fallback. Explicit turn-off entries remain off even when the new template could use that fixture. Explicit preserve entries protect their marked original appearance and illumination. Apply the emitted-light changes and their related bounce/reflections coherently within the rebuilt setup. Preserve marks are generative constraints, not pixel masks or a promise of exact compositing.

LOCAL.BASELINE: Use the selected custom or legacy lighting treatment as the starting point for this existing scene. Treat image 1 as the lighting baseline, then execute any explicit original-light handling and optional local edits. Infer its actual original artificial sources, daylight direction, shadow softness, exposure range and white balance from the clean image. Whole-scene original-light handling needs no user marks or separate detection image. Preserve the existing interior design style, material colors, time of day and weather. Adapt the treatment to actual window brightness, room depth, surface reflectance, highlights and dark areas rather than fixed lamp positions, a fixed exposure or a style-wide tint. Existing original lights may be kept, dimmed or switched off only according to the explicit original-light operation and single-light edits; new requested fill remains independent. Different design styles do not imply a mandatory bright or dark exposure.
LOCAL.HARDWARE: Retain the physical bodies, positions and material identities of original lamps, strips and luminous panels when keeping, dimming or switching off their emission. Whole-scene original-light handling does not add, remove or replace hardware and must not fabricate new emitters. Legacy scene templates adapt to real visible windows, existing fixtures and surfaces; if a legacy template lacks a plausible source, use a restrained source-consistent fallback that never reactivates a source explicitly switched off. Manually marked new lights supply their specified geometry, target, mode, Kelvin intent and brightness. Only an explicit ADD FIXTURE AND LIGHT entry may add its requested physical luminaire; original-light handling does not switch off this newly added luminaire or its contribution.
LOCAL.RECONCILE: Reconcile explicit original-light handling and optional marked edits on their physically affected surfaces, with a coherent key/fill hierarchy, realistic occlusion, contact shadows, falloff and material reflections. Whole-scene original-light darken or turn-off addresses original artificial emitters across image 1 without requiring marks; single-light refinements affect only their identified source. Retain source bodies and preserve daylight and exterior natural illumination. Apply emission changes and their attributable bounce/reflections, never a global exposure reduction, painted dark overlay or arbitrary receiving-area dimming. Original-light keep maintains original emission states as a baseline, while independent new light can still illuminate those fixtures and nearby surfaces. Explicit off has priority over dimming and must not be undone by rebalancing, fill or prose; current-request new illumination remains independent and does not reopen an original emitter. Preserve marks remain highest priority. Avoid contradictory duplicate shadows or arbitrary warm/cool splits; keep the original white balance rather than tinting the whole room. Preserve marks are generative constraints, not pixel masks or exact compositing.

SCOPE.REBUILD: LIGHTING QUALITY SCOPE: apply the following professional lighting and photographic finish across the rebuilt setup while preserving the selected template's distinct key direction, exposure family and intentional shadow design. Explicit edits and PRESERVE marks take priority over all quality refinements. Template ratios describe a visual lighting hierarchy, not calibrated photometry.
SCOPE.LOCAL: LIGHTING QUALITY SCOPE: apply the following photographic finish within the explicit original-light handling and optional local edits, their attributable receiving surfaces, and the chosen custom or legacy treatment. Preserve its daylight direction, white balance, exposure intent and protection boundaries. Do not use quality refinement to reset the whole room, undo original-light keep/dim/off, change unrelated fixture states or weaken requested new illumination. Explicit original-light and single-light darken, turn-off and PRESERVE actions remain binding; retain readable detail through the actual remaining and newly requested illumination rather than a blanket exposure correction.

PHOTOGRAPHY.LIGHTING_QUALITY: PHOTOGRAPHIC LIGHTING QUALITY: use one coherent motivated key and broad soft supporting fill wherever the selected lighting treatment permits it. Keep the principal furniture and key wall/floor surfaces readable through continuous exposure and physically plausible falloff within each intended lighting zone. Remove accidental bright/dark blotches, abrupt illumination gaps, locally burned-white patches, circular light blobs and unexplained spotty pools. Even illumination does not mean equal brightness across the whole image: retain designed key/fill contrast, projected shadows, focal hierarchy, intentional dark regions and nighttime ambience. Supporting fill reveals detail without creating a competing key direction or washing out the template's lighting character. Never counteract an explicit darken/off/protect edit to satisfy this quality target.
PHOTOGRAPHY.MATERIAL_TONAL: MATERIAL AND TONAL RENDERING: retain every visible object and small prop's category, construction, identity and distinguishing features. Do not replace existing objects or add decorative props merely for photographic styling, and do not turn steam, reflections or other optical phenomena into new physical objects. Retain real-scale leather grain and creases, stone mineral texture and polish/roughness, textile weave and fibers, and metal directional roughness appropriate to the visible source surfaces. Preserve intrinsic material colors and existing surface patterns rather than adding invented decorative grain. Use physically credible source-dependent reflections, roughness-dependent highlight spread and contact shadows that seat objects on their surfaces. Give highlights a smooth roll-off, retain useful shadow detail, natural midtones and restrained local contrast. Avoid waxy or plastic-looking surfaces, smeared materials, excessive microtexture, sharpening halos, clipped specular patches, grey HDR haze and whole-image color filters. Maintain natural photographic color separation and believable material response without oversaturation.
PHOTOGRAPHY.CAMERA_OPTICS: CAMERA AND OPTICAL CHARACTER: use the user-specified Canon R1 camera profile below, with natural color fidelity, smooth tonal gradation, material separation and restrained optical clarity. Apply the requested 24mm lens character while preserving the source camera viewpoint, framing, perspective, object scale and spatial proportions. Do not pull the camera back, widen the room, tilt verticals or distort architecture to simulate an impressive photograph. Render the appearance of a naturally merged bracketed HDR photograph, retaining undistorted shadow detail and unclipped highlights without grey HDR haze, halos or flat local contrast. Keep clean, credible detail without artificial edge enhancement or a new depth-of-field effect that hides scene detail. Return one final photograph, not separate bracketed exposures or an exposure collage.

WHITE_BALANCE.REBUILD: Choose a white balance appropriate to the selected new lighting scheme, then lock it consistently across the exposure bracket. This does not mean inheriting the original image's white balance.
WHITE_BALANCE.LOCAL: Keep the established white balance of the custom or legacy lighting treatment and lock it consistently across the exposure bracket; do not reset unrelated scene lighting.

INTRO.REBUILD: Relight image 1 by rebuilding its illumination for the selected lighting template. Use the clean original as scene reference while replacing its lighting, shadows and light-induced reflections.
INTRO.LOCAL: Relight image 1 using the explicit original-light operation, if present, and the selected custom or legacy treatment with optional marked edits. Infer original artificial emitters directly from the clean scene; whole-scene original-light handling does not require a guide image.

INPUT.PLAIN: Image 1 is the only scene input. There is no manual lighting guide or additional reference image.
INPUT.GUIDED: The numbered lighting plan in image 2 supplies explicit local edits. Image 2 is the same scene with temporary colored shapes and numbered action symbols. Each number maps only to the corresponding action below; image 1 remains the only source of scene appearance.

ADAPTER.REBUILD_GUIDE: Use image 2 only to read the explicit guide marks. Its underlying old illumination is not a target for the rebuilt lighting.
ADAPTER.GUIDE_LEGEND: GUIDE LEGEND: blue + means ADD NEW LIGHT (BRIGHTEN) and has an arrow from the new source toward its receiving surface. Purple - means DIM EXISTING LIGHT: identify the actual existing luminaire or finite emitting segment touched by the mark and reduce only its emitted contribution. Red x means TURN OFF the marked identifiable existing emitter while keeping its body; green = means PRESERVE the marked scene content and its illumination. Darken and turn-off marks locate existing emitters, not new sources or receiving-area masks; if no existing emitter is identifiable, leave the scene unchanged by that action and do not darken the marked surface as a fallback. Only new-light marks have direction arrows. Guide colors and symbols are unrelated to light colors. Infer plausible 3D orientation from visible surfaces and perspective; screen coordinates express user intent, not measured world coordinates.

SCENE_CONSTRAINT.REBUILD: Preserve the camera viewpoint, framing, architecture, furniture, object positions, intrinsic material colors and surface patterns. Recompute illumination-dependent shadows, indirect bounce and reflections for the chosen new setup; do not copy the original light distribution. Existing fixtures keep their physical bodies, but their emitted brightness, color and on/off states may change as required by the template. Explicit marked edits and PRESERVE regions take priority. Avoid blown highlights, crushed detail and a whole-image color filter. Light-only entries must not create visible fixtures; only explicit fixture entries may add their specified luminaire.
SCENE_CONSTRAINT.LOCAL: Preserve the camera viewpoint, framing, architecture, furniture, object positions, material identities and surface patterns. Execute explicit original-light keep/dim/off on identifiable original artificial luminaires and their attributable bounce and reflections, preserving their bodies and natural daylight. Keep original emission states as a baseline only when keep is selected or no original-light operation was requested; explicit dim/off overrides that baseline. Whole-scene handling uses the original image directly and requires no marks. Single-light marks remain restricted to their identifiable original emitter; if no emitter is identifiable, leave the scene unchanged by that action instead of darkening the marked receiving surface. If no original artificial emitters exist for whole-scene handling, do not force the room darker. New illumination and newly requested visible fixtures are independent of original-light handling. Light-only additions must not create physical fixtures; only explicit new fixture entries may add their specified luminaire. Explicit off must not be undone by dimming, fill, photography refinement or prose, while preserve marks retain priority. Avoid global exposure dimming, whole-image filters, painted dark regions, blown highlights or blocked detail as substitutes for physically related emission changes.

OUTPUT.PLAIN: Return one complete photorealistic scene image without labels, diagrams, overlays, borders, collages or newly invented lighting hardware.
OUTPUT.GUIDED: Return one complete photorealistic scene image. Remove all temporary blue marks and purple, red or green marks, source outlines, numbers, symbols, arrows, labels and overlays. Do not render guide shapes as visible light beams or add a diagram, border or collage.
